title: Fine-grained microbatch governor with KV-reserve and soft-failover under sustained QPS
creator: Asha Nair
description:
Problem: Under sustained high QPS we observe noisy latency spikes and occasional OOMs caused by KV cache growth combined with aggressive microbatching that assumes headroom which vanishes under multi-tenant pressure. Existing admission controllers use coarse token-slot ceilings and reactive eviction that causes oscillation in p95 latency and increased tail variance.

Goal: Implement a fine-grained microbatch governor that: 1) reserves a small configurable KV memory buffer per tenant (KV-reserve) to prevent catastrophic cross-tenant eviction, 2) performs slot-level soft-throttling based on a latency SLO signal and predictive headroom estimator, and 3) provides a soft-failover path (graceful degrade) when sustained pressure is detected (reduce kv_retention, increase quantization for fallback model variant, temporarily narrow batching window). The aim is to preserve p95 latency SLOs while avoiding OOM-driven outages and keeping throughput loss < 15% in steady-state high QPS bursts.

Approach summary:
- Admission controller enhancement: Replace a single global microbatch threshold with a two-tier governor: (a) per-tenant token-slot budgets (lease tokens) that are replenished by a predictive replenishment algorithm (EWMA of recent consumption + surge factor), and (b) a short-window soft-throttle that applies a proportional reduction when the p95 latency delta exceeds threshold.
- KV-reserve: Maintain a small per-tenant reserved KV slab (configurable, default 5% of KV heap) that is protected from global eviction. When KV pressure goes beyond threshold, the controller transitions to soft-failover rather than immediate eviction of protected slab.
- Predictive headroom estimator: Lightweight estimator that consumes recent request size distribution and GPU free slab telemetry to predict headroom for next 10s window. Used to make admission decisions and to time preemptive KV compact/eviction.
- Soft-failover paths: staged degradations prioritized to minimize user-visible regressions: (1) drop batching window by X ms, (2) lower kv_retention policy for cold entries, (3) switch low-priority requests to quantized-variant model (same semantics, lower memory), (4) last resort: reject low-priority requests with clear error code and throttling advice.
- GPU memory management: tighten slab allocator watermarks (low/critical) and trigger asynchronous compaction on headroom prediction rather than only on reactive failure. Also add a short-lived slab loan pool to absorb microbursts without impacting KV slab immediately.

Trade-offs considered:
- Reserving KV memory per tenant reduces global KV cache efficiency but prevents tenant eviction storms and noisy neighbor OOMs — acceptable for enterprise SLAs.
- Predictive approaches risk false positives (over-conservative throttling) — mitigated by tuning EWMA half-life and using p95 delta feedback to adapt sensitivity.
- Graceful degrade ordering chosen to prefer latency-preserving steps over throughput-preserving ones because user experience prioritizes tail latency in our SLOs.

Telemetry & observability: New metrics to emit: governor/replenish_rate, governor/reserve_usage_by_tenant, governor/p95_delta, governor/predicted_headroom, governor/failover_stage, slab/compaction_trigger, slab/loan_pool_usage. Dashboards and alerts will be added to runtime-1.21 Grafana.

Docs & artifacts: design doc -> https://redwood.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/RUNTIME/pages/56789012/Fine-grained+Microbatch+Governor ; initial perf runbook -> https://drive.redwood.ai/drive/folders/1aB2cPerfRunbook ; prototype PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/1420
acceptance_criteria:
1) Deployed feature flag guarded on canary pool and non-customer-facing endpoints.
2) p95 latency under synthetic sustained QPS (3x baseline) improves by >= 30% compared to current controller and p99 does not regress > 10%.
3) No OOMs in 2 hour stress-run on multi-tenant bench with KV working set = 1.4x available slab.
4) Throughput drop measured in steady state < 15% vs baseline under same test.
5) New Grafana panels populated and alerts firing on regressions.
6) Documentation updated (design + runbook) and 2 SRE engineers runbook-reviewed.
7) Integration tests cover soft-failover transitions and per-tenant reserve honoring.
